answer: A work-backed admission fee stops a sybil swarm at its cheapest point: joining. Each new identity must stake a bond locked for a fixed tenure and prove real inference work whose receipts peers verify. To mint N identities an attacker pays N bonds plus N times the compute bill, and every fabricated receipt sits at a ledge of rejection risk. Only honest work turns a bare vertex of trust into a durable one. Sybils thus cost real money and earn little, so forgery loses its edge; price entry in slow ivory-clean capital, not free signups.
